item.title: Israel intentionally released footage of Mossad operatives in Iran to provoke mass arrests, ex-chief says
item.description:
Israel intentionally released footage of Mossad operatives in Iran to provoke mass arrests, ex-chief says

Submitted by MEE staff on Sun, 11/01/2026 - 11:20
David Barnea says Mossad published video during the 12-day war to overwhelm Iranian agencies, making it difficult to distinguish operatives from ordinary citizens
A screengrab from a social media video shows cars set on fire during a protest at Saadat Abad Square in Tehran, 9 January 2026 (UGC/AFP)
Off

Former Mossad chief David Barnea has said Israel intentionally released images of their covert operation in Iran during the June 2025 conflict to provoke mass arrests and make it harder for Iranian forces to find real Israeli agents.

“One of the reasons we immediately released an official video on the morning of Operation Rising Lion, with the Mossad logo, was to protect the agents who were there,” Barnea said, according to comments The Jerusalem Post reported on 25 October.

Barnea said the leak of the footage of Israeli operations in Iran was not just an attempt to showcase the Mossad’s reach but also a strategy to overwhelm Iranian counterintelligence, causing them to make mass arrests, making it more difficult to distinguish operatives from ordinary citizens.

“We wanted to make sure they arrested so many people in Iran that they wouldn’t be able to distinguish the wheat from the chaff and would eventually release everyone,” he said.

Barnea said Iranian authorities arrested 21,000 people during the operation.

“You have to imagine that when you arrest 21,000 people, even if you’ve caught an agent or two, eventually you have to release them because everyone’s story will be the same: I was walking down the street, I was driving a car, they arrested me,” he said.

Barnea added that many people arrested or executed on accusations of working for Israel had no connection to the Mossad.

Read More »

“Some of the people being hanged in Iran on accusations of being Mossad agents, I have to ask who they are,” he said. “They tell me, ‘Listen, we don’t know either.’”

He described some of those executed as “just unfortunate people whom they decided were our agents, but who never worked for the Mossad, and probably never worked for any other intelligence organisation either”, according to the reported remarks.

The remarks made at the Priority Summit on 22 October to a private audience have sparked a sharp response from Trita Parsi.

Parsi, executive vice-president of the Quincy Institute for Responsible Statecraft, described it as an admission that Israel "used ordinary Iranians as tools to protect Mossad operatives" in the country.

“Rarely will you find a more crude admission of how Israel deliberately and carelessly put thousands of people it claimed it sought to liberate in harm’s way,” Parsi wrote on X.

Mass detentions

Israel launched Operation Rising Lion on 13 June 2025, during which they bombed Iran and killed senior military commanders as well as scientists.

After Iran retaliated with missile attacks on Israel, the 12-day war ended with a ceasefire.

On the first morning of the attacks, the Mossad released videos showing what it said were its agents operating inside Iran.

Iranian official says at least 5,000 killed in protests
Read More »

The footage included attacks on ballistic missile and air-defence targets, with the faces of those involved concealed.

Iranian police announced in August 2025 that they had detained about 21,000 people during the 12-day conflict.

Police spokesperson Saeed Montazer al-Mahdi said the arrests followed reports from members of the public and increased security measures.

More than 260 suspects were arrested on suspicion of espionage and 172 people were arrested for illegal filming, the police statement said.

Barnea’s comments come amid concerns over Iran’s use of espionage allegations to prosecute people following the conflict.

Amnesty International and Human Rights Watch said in September 2025 that Iranian authorities had arrested more than 20,000 people after the outbreak of hostilities with Israel.

Those targeted included journalists, human rights activists, social media users, members of ethnic and religious minorities, and foreigners.

Iranian authorities have said they were responding to genuine threats from Israeli intelligence and collaborators inside the country.

Tehran has repeatedly accused the Mossad of recruiting people to gather intelligence, carry out sabotage and assist military attacks.

Qatar condemns tanker attack in the Gulf as threat to global energy security
item.description:
Qatar condemns tanker attack in the Gulf as threat to global energy security

Qatar has condemned an attack on one of its tankers as a "dangerous escalation" that threatens global energy security and maritime navigation.

In a foreign ministry statement, Doha warned of the dangers posed by "reckless and irresponsible practices" of attacking tankers.

“The Ministry of Foreign Affairs affirms that the State of Qatar reserves its right to take all necessary measures – in accordance with the provisions of international law and the Charter of the United Nations – to protect its property, safeguard its interests, and ensure the safety of its ships and crews," said the Qatari foreign ministry.  

Earlier, the Qatar Gas Transport Company Limited said its vessel was hit by “unidentified objects” while sailing in the Gulf on Friday.

item.title: Iran submits evidence of US-Israeli attacks on maritime infrastructure to IMO
item.description:
Iran submits evidence of US-Israeli attacks on maritime infrastructure to IMO

Iran said it has submitted evidence of US and Israeli attacks on its maritime infrastructure to the International Maritime Organisation (IMO).

The dossier of evidence given by Tehran to the IMO includes documents and photographic evidence of sabotage on its maritime infrastructure.

An Iranian official said IMO member states will discuss the evidence at a council session taking place in London on 2-6 November.

The attacks on its maritime infrastructure, according to Iran, threaten the safety of international shipping and seafarers. 

Iran's IRNA news agency reported that damage to maritime traffic control systems also increases the risk of accidents, and the destruction of rescue facilities undermines emergency response capabilities.

Yamaha to skip Qatar Grand Prix over security concerns
item.description:
Yamaha to skip Qatar Grand Prix over security concerns

Yamaha will not participate in the Qatar Grand Prix of MotoGP, after concerns over the country's security situation.

In a statement, MotoGP said it was disappointed by Yamaha's decision, but noted that the company decided to not change its "company-wide travel restrictions".

"MotoGP is disappointed by Yamaha's decision not to participate in the Qatar Grand Prix. While we recognise the team is subject to a broader corporate policy restricting travel to the Middle East, we do not believe this decision reflects the extensive assurances provided to all championship stakeholders," said MotoGP in a statement.

"Following consultation with the State of Qatar, Lusail International Circuit, independent safety advisers and MotoGP's own ongoing risk assessment process, MotoGP has not received any information that would warrant a change to the current plans for the event."

item.title: Israeli army builds new roads linking military posts in southern Lebanon
item.description: The Israeli army is building new roads through mountains and valleys in southern Lebanon to connect its military positions, Lebanon’s National News Agency (NNA) reported Saturday, Anadolu reports. The work spans the western and central sectors of southern Lebanon, where Israeli forces have established military posts on occupied Lebanese territory, according to the agency. NNA said the construction was taking place alongside Israeli demolition operations in the area. The central sector includes the towns of Aita al-Shaab, Maroun al-Ras, Bint Jbeil and Aitaroun. Maroun al-Ras overlooks the Israeli settlement of Avivim across the border.
